newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may shut more overseas outposts -paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may shut more overseas outposts -paper.

text.p: Taipei, which recently severed unofficial ties with Cambodia and cited arch-rival China as the reason, may shut down more overseas representative offices, a local newspaper reported on Sunday.
The foreign ministry was mulling closing its unofficial outposts that serve more "symbolic" than real diplomatic purposes, the Independence Evening Post quoted unnamed ministry sources as saying.
The newspaper did not say which offices Taipei may close and the ministry could not be reached immediately for comment.
Taipei on Monday withdrew its representatives from Phnom Penh and ordered Cambodia's Taipei office closed.

Cambodian strongman Hun Sen on July 22 had ordered the closing of Taiwan's office, alleging Taiwanese interference in his bloody early July showdown with the forces of royalist co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Taipei has denied complicity in Cambodia's political turmoil and laid the blame for the row squarely with communist China, saying Beijing was calling the shots in Phnom Penh and now was widening its long-time diplomatic embargo of Taiwan to non-official spheres.
Beijing, rivals with Taipei since they were split by a civil war in 1949, considers Taiwan a renegade province not entitled to foreign contacts.
Taiwan currently has formal diplomatic ties with only 30 countries -- mostly poor states dependent on the wealthy island for economic succour.
It maintains unofficial relations with most other countries, including vibrant trade links with economic powers like the United States, Japan and even mainland China.
